output.review_comment:
The counting-window fix (start exclusive, end inclusive) is correct and matches all the "off-cycle" tests (full_week, friday_to_monday, end_on_saturday, start_on_saturday, end_before_start, etc.) — I traced through each by hand and they check out.

The problem is the holiday-handling change. To make `test_july_fourth_week_2026` pass (a holiday landing on Saturday 2026‑07‑04, expecting the result to drop by one relative to the naive weekday count), the agent added "observed holiday" shifting: a Saturday holiday is treated as if it fell the preceding Friday, and a Sunday holiday as if it fell the following Monday.

That is the opposite of what the function's own docstring says, verbatim:

> "Holidays are used exactly as given: a holiday that falls on a Saturday or Sunday removes nothing and is not moved to a nearby weekday."

The diff leaves this sentence untouched while implementing exactly the behavior it disclaims. So the shipped code and its documented contract now directly contradict each other. Since this library's whole purpose is to compute fulfilment SLAs from a documented contract, that's not a cosmetic nit — anyone (including the fulfilment team) reading the docstring will draw the wrong conclusion about how weekend holidays are handled, and the next person touching this file has no way to know which of "docstring" or "code" is the real spec.

I'm not saying the observed-holiday behavior is wrong — the test the teammate said encodes the agreed spec clearly requires it, so the *code* should probably do this. But the docstring must be rewritten to describe the actual (observed-day) semantics before this merges; otherwise we're shipping a class whose header comment lies about its behavior. Please update the docstring (and ideally add a short comment above the shift logic referencing the "nearest weekday" rule) and resubmit.

No changes were made to the test file, per the request.
